title: Psalms Chapter 88 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Psalms chapter 88 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Psalms Chapter 88 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Psalms Chapter 88.

questions.question: Who is the Psalm 88 attributed to in its heading?
questions.explanation: The heading of Psalm 88 states it is a Maschil of Heman the Ezrahite (Psalms 88:1).

questions.question: According to Psalms 88, how often does the psalmist cry out to the LORD?
questions.explanation: The psalmist says, 'I have cried day and night before thee' (Psalms 88:1).

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do with his prayer in Psalms 88?
options: Let my prayer come before thee
questions.correctAnswer: Let my prayer come before thee
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:2, the psalmist asks, 'Let my prayer come before thee: incline thine ear unto my cry;'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 88 says the psalmist's soul is full of troubles.
questions.explanation: Verse 3 states, 'For my soul is full of troubles;'

questions.question: What does the psalmist say his life is drawing near to in Psalms 88?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:3 says, 'and my life draweth nigh unto the grave.'

questions.question: In Psalms 88, with whom is the psalmist counted?
options: Them that go down into the pit
questions.correctAnswer: Them that go down into the pit
questions.explanation: Verse 4 states, 'I am counted with them that go down into the pit.'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 88, the psalmist is as a man that hath great strength.
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:4 says, 'I am as a man that hath no strength;'

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his state among the dead in Psalms 88?
questions.explanation: Verse 5 states, 'Free among the dead, like the slain that lie in the grave,'

questions.question: What does the psalmist say about God's remembrance of the dead in Psalms 88?
options: God keeps them in His heart
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:5 says, 'whom thou rememberest no more.'

questions.question: Where has God laid the psalmist according to Psalms 88?
options: In the lowest pit, in darkness, in the deeps
questions.correctAnswer: In the lowest pit, in darkness, in the deeps
questions.explanation: Verse 6 says, 'Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit, in darkness, in the deeps.'

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 88 says the psalmist's eye mourns because of affliction.
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:9 states, 'Mine eye mourneth by reason of affliction;'

questions.question: What has the LORD done to the psalmist's acquaintance in Psalms 88?
questions.explanation: Verse 8 says, 'Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me;'

questions.question: In Psalms 88, what is the psalmist's condition from his youth up?
questions.explanation: Verse 15 states, 'I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up:'

questions.question: True or False: According to Psalms 88, the psalmist has called upon the LORD only occasionally.
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:9 says, 'LORD, I have called daily upon thee,' indicating frequent calling.

questions.question: In Psalms 88, which of the following comes first in the psalmist's experience?
options: The psalmist cries day and night
The psalmist is laid in the lowest pit
The psalmist is afflicted and ready to die
questions.correctAnswer: The psalmist cries day and night
questions.explanation: The psalmist first cries day and night (verse 1) before being laid in the lowest pit (verse 6) and before expressions of mourning and affliction later in the chapter.

medium.title: Psalms Chapter 88 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Psalms Chapter 88 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about his condition in Psalms 88:3?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states that 'For my soul is full of troubles' indicating his deep distress and turmoil. (Psalms 88:3)

questions.question: According to Psalms 88:7, what has afflicted the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The psalmist mentions, 'Thy wrath lieth hard upon me,' indicating that he feels burdened by God's anger. (Psalms 88:7)

questions.question: What does Psalms 88:8 reveal about the psalmist's relationships?
options: He is in a joyful reunion
questions.explanation: The verse states, 'Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me,' showing his feeling of isolation. (Psalms 88:8)

questions.question: How does the psalmist express his prayer life in Psalms 88:9?
options: He calls daily upon the Lord
questions.correctAnswer: He calls daily upon the Lord
questions.explanation: The psalmist says, 'I have called daily upon thee,' emphasizing his persistent prayer despite his suffering. (Psalms 88:9)

questions.question: What question does the psalmist ask in Psalms 88:10 regarding the dead?
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee?' indicating his despair about the afterlife. (Psalms 88:10)

questions.question: In Psalms 88:11, what does the psalmist question about God's lovingkindness?
options: It is declared in the grave
It is only for the living
questions.correctAnswer: It is declared in the grave
questions.explanation: The verse questions, 'Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave?' expressing doubt about God's faithfulness after death. (Psalms 88:11)

questions.question: According to Psalms 88:12, where does the psalmist suggest God's wonders should be known?
options: In the land of the living
questions.explanation: The psalmist asks, 'Shall thy wonders be known in the dark?' which indicates a longing for God's presence even in despair. (Psalms 88:12)

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist feels that God has completely abandoned him.
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses feelings of abandonment, saying 'Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me.' (Psalms 88:8)

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist experiences joy and comfort during his affliction.
questions.explanation: The psalmist indicates he is 'ready to die' and is 'distracted' by his suffering, showing he is not experiencing comfort. (Psalms 88:15)

questions.question: What does Psalms 88:14 reveal about the psalmist's feelings toward God?
questions.explanation: The psalmist cries out, 'LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?' revealing his deep sense of abandonment. (Psalms 88:14)

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his suffering from youth in Psalms 88:15?
options: He is afflicted and ready to die
questions.correctAnswer: He is afflicted and ready to die
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up,' indicating a long history of suffering. (Psalms 88:15)

questions.question: What metaphor does the psalmist use to describe his situation in Psalms 88:6?
options: A man in the lowest pit
questions.correctAnswer: A man in the lowest pit
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses, 'Thou hast laid me in the lowest pit,' illustrating his sense of despair and hopelessness. (Psalms 88:6)

questions.question: What does Psalms 88:16 say about the psalmist's experience with God's wrath?
questions.explanation: The psalmist states, 'Thy fierce wrath goeth over me; thy terrors have cut me off,' indicating the devastating effect of God's wrath on him. (Psalms 88:16)

questions.question: What imagery does the psalmist use in Psalms 88:17 to describe his affliction?
questions.explanation: The psalmist describes his affliction as being 'compassed about daily like water,' suggesting a feeling of being overwhelmed. (Psalms 88:17)

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist believes that God is present in his darkest moments.
questions.explanation: The psalmist feels abandoned and questions God's presence, suggesting he does not believe God is with him in his darkest moments. (Psalms 88:14)

hard.title: Psalms Chapter 88 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Psalms Chapter 88.

questions.question: According to Psalms 88:13, when does the psalmist say his prayer will reach the LORD?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:13 states, 'But unto thee have I cried, O LORD; and in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee,' indicating the prayer reaches the LORD in the morning.

questions.question: In Psalms 88:14, the psalmist questions why God has done what to his soul?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:14 says, 'LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?' showing the psalmist feels forsaken.

questions.question: What condition does the psalmist describe about himself in Psalms 88:15?
options: Afflicted and ready to die from youth up
questions.correctAnswer: Afflicted and ready to die from youth up
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:15 declares, 'I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up,' indicating lifelong suffering.

questions.question: In Psalms 88:16, what has cut the psalmist off?
questions.explanation: The verse says, 'Thy fierce wrath goeth over me; thy terrors have cut me off,' showing divine terrors as the cause.

questions.question: How does the psalmist describe his troubles in Psalms 88:17?
options: Coming round about daily like water
questions.correctAnswer: Coming round about daily like water
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:17 states, 'They came round about me daily like water; they compassed me about together,' illustrating overwhelming troubles.

questions.question: What has the LORD done to the psalmist's lover, friend, and acquaintance according to Psalms 88:18?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:18 reads, 'Lover and friend hast thou put far from me, and mine acquaintance into darkness,' describing isolation.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of being cast off and hidden by God as expressed in Psalms 88:14?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 49:14 expresses a feeling of being forsaken by God, paralleling the psalmist's cry in Psalms 88:14 about God's hidden face.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Psalms 88:17 where troubles are described as coming 'like water' and encompassing the psalmist?
questions.explanation: The phrase 'like water' in Psalms 88:17 uses a simile to compare troubles to water surrounding the psalmist.

questions.question: The Hebrew word often translated as 'afflicted' in Psalms 88:15 (עָנָה - 'anah') primarily means what?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root עָנָה ('anah') means to be humbled or oppressed, fitting the psalmist’s description of suffering in Psalms 88:15.

questions.question: According to Psalms 88:13-14, the psalmist's persistent crying to the LORD in the morning contrasts with what feeling expressed in verse 14?
options: Feeling cast off and hidden from God
questions.correctAnswer: Feeling cast off and hidden from God
questions.explanation: Verses 13 and 14 together show the psalmist’s persistent prayer contrasted with his feeling that God has cast him off and hidden His face.

questions.question: What cultural or historical context helps explain the psalmist's description of being 'laid in the lowest pit' and 'in darkness' in Psalms 88:6?
options: Ancient Near Eastern imagery of Sheol as a dark underworld
questions.correctAnswer: Ancient Near Eastern imagery of Sheol as a dark underworld
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:6 uses imagery common in the Ancient Near East where Sheol, or the realm of the dead, was viewed as a dark, deep pit.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage reflects a similar theme of persistent prayer amidst suffering like Psalms 88:13?
questions.explanation: Luke 18:1-8 teaches the importance of persistent prayer, echoing the psalmist's cry in Psalms 88:13 to continually seek God despite affliction.

questions.question: True or False: Psalms 88:15 states that the psalmist has only recently begun to suffer God's terrors.
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:15 says, 'I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up,' indicating the suffering is lifelong, not recent.

questions.question: True or False: The psalmist in Psalms 88 feels completely isolated, including from his closest friends and family.
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:18 confirms that the psalmist’s lover, friend, and acquaintance have been put far from him, indicating deep isolation.

questions.question: Which Psalm shares a thematic connection to Psalms 88 regarding lament and persistent calling upon God in distress?
questions.explanation: Psalm 42, like Psalm 88, expresses deep distress and persistent longing for God amidst suffering, making it thematically connected.

theological.title: Psalms Chapter 88 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Psalms Chapter 88 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What is the primary emotion expressed by the psalmist in Psalms 88?
questions.explanation: The psalmist expresses deep sorrow and despair throughout the chapter, highlighting his struggles and afflictions. This is evident in verses like Psalms 88:3, where he states, 'For my soul is full of troubles.'

questions.question: Which attribute of God is primarily highlighted in Psalms 88:1?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:1 refers to God as 'the God of my salvation,' emphasizing His role as a savior and deliverer, which is a central attribute of God.

questions.question: What does the psalmist ask God to do in Psalms 88:2?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:2, the psalmist pleads, 'Let my prayer come before thee: incline thine ear unto my cry,' requesting God's attention to his prayer.

questions.question: What metaphor does the psalmist use to describe his state in Psalms 88:4?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:4, the psalmist states, 'I am as a man that hath no strength,' indicating his deep sense of weakness and despair.

questions.question: According to Psalms 88:5, how does the psalmist feel about his condition?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:5 mentions, 'whom thou rememberest no more,' indicating the psalmist's feeling of being forsaken and forgotten by God.

questions.question: What does the psalmist acknowledge about God's actions in Psalms 88:7?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:7, the psalmist states, 'Thy wrath lieth hard upon me,' acknowledging God's anger and affliction in his life.

questions.question: What does the psalmist express about his relationships in Psalms 88:8?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:8 reveals, 'Thou hast put away mine acquaintance far from me,' indicating that the psalmist feels isolated and distanced from others.

questions.question: What question does the psalmist pose in Psalms 88:10 regarding the dead?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:10, the psalmist asks, 'Wilt thou shew wonders to the dead? shall the dead arise and praise thee?' indicating a concern about the dead's ability to praise God.

questions.question: In Psalms 88:11, what aspect of God does the psalmist question?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:11 asks, 'Shall thy lovingkindness be declared in the grave?' questioning if God's love can reach beyond death.

questions.question: What does Psalms 88:13 reveal about the psalmist's attitude towards prayer?
options: He prays only in the morning
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:13, the psalmist states, 'But unto thee have I cried, O LORD; and in the morning shall my prayer prevent thee,' indicating his continuous and persistent prayer.

questions.question: What deep struggle does the psalmist express in Psalms 88:14?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:14 shows the psalmist asking, 'LORD, why castest thou off my soul? why hidest thou thy face from me?' reflecting feelings of abandonment by God.

questions.question: What does the psalmist describe as his condition in Psalms 88:15?
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:15 states, 'I am afflicted and ready to die from my youth up,' indicating his long-standing suffering and despair.

questions.question: How does the psalmist depict his afflictions in Psalms 88:16?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:16, the psalmist states, 'Thy fierce wrath goeth over me; thy terrors have cut me off,' illustrating his afflictions as overwhelming burdens.

questions.question: What imagery does the psalmist use in Psalms 88:17 to describe his afflictions?
questions.explanation: In Psalms 88:17, the psalmist describes his afflictions as 'They came round about me daily like water,' signifying the overwhelming nature of his struggles.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God is distant and unresponsive to human suffering. What does Psalms 88:14-15 actually teach?
options: God is involved in human pain
God ignores the cries of the afflicted
questions.correctAnswer: God is involved in human pain
questions.explanation: Psalms 88:14-15 reveals the psalmist's deep cry to God amidst his afflictions, showing that he seeks God's presence and acknowledges his suffering, thus indicating that God is engaged with human pain.
